page: Amazon Web Services c7a.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 3031.18. However, because the instance is limited to a single vCPU, its multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a poor read-only small block cached speed of 147.72 GB/sec, while large block write bandwidth remains average at 28.35 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels.

The c7a.medium offers a low-cost entry point into the dedicated AMD EPYC Zen 4 architecture, providing high single-core efficiency without the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances. However, the lack of local storage, 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and poor multi-core scaling present significant tradeoffs. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput all rank in the bottom 10% of benchmarks. Consequently, this instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, or small-scale development workloads that require dedicated CPU execution but do not demand high memory capacity or parallel processing.
